title: Big bands at the Michigan and Paradise theatres
summary: Seeing Sinatra with Dorsey and the Black bands, including Basie, Hines with Eckstine and Sarah Vaughan, at the Paradise.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: There was plenty of good listening around the city during that period. I remember going down to the Michigan Theatre. That's where I first heard Frank Sinatra with the Tommy Dorsey Orchestra. That was a real treat. And Timmy Rogers was on the bill, the comedian and musician; he was on the bill. That was an exciting show.

They also had a theatre, the Paradise Theatre, where all the name Black bands would play -- Ellington, Lunceford, Andy Kirk. A lot of different acts. Cab Calloway. I first saw Count Basie in the Paradise. And I first saw Earl Fatha Hines when he came to Detroit, and I heard Billy Eckstine with him at the time, and also Sarah Vaughan, Charlie Parker
Dizzy Gillespie -- that hand. Hell, that was a real monster he had there, that particular band.
